The canonical EIN format

Source: R/md-ein.R
md_ein.Rd

Every key in matchdb is an EIN2 - EIN-XX-XXXXXXX, e.g. EIN-00-0019818. This is the stable identifier used across the e-file data series, the BMF, and the NCCS metadata crosswalks, and matchdb adopts it so joins across those sources need no conversion step in which a leading zero can be lost.

md_is_ein() tests for the canonical form without converting.

Usage

md_ein(x, to = c("id", "n"), strict = TRUE)

md_is_ein(x)

Arguments

x

Character or numeric vector of EINs in any mixed format - "123456789", "12-3456789", "EIN-12-3456789", "ein-12-3456789".

to

"id" for EIN-XX-XXXXXXX, "n" for nine bare digits.

strict

Return NA rather than truncating when the digit count is not nine. Defaults to TRUE.

Value

A character vector, NA where the input could not be represented.

Details

Leading zeros are the whole reason for the format. 00-0019818 read as a number is 19818, and an EIN column that has passed through a spreadsheet or an untyped CSV read is a well known way to lose organisations whose EIN begins with zero. A string that cannot be coerced to a number cannot be silently renumbered.

Semantics follow ef2::format_ein(), which is the upstream definition, with one deliberate difference described below. matchdb does not depend on ef2 - it is an ETL pipeline rather than a library - so the function is reimplemented in base R and tested against ef2's documented examples.

Strictness

ef2::format_ein() strips non-digits and pads to nine characters, then takes substr(x, 1, 2) and substr(x, 3, 9). An input carrying more than nine digits is therefore silently truncated: "12345678901" becomes "EIN-12-3456789", with the trailing digits discarded and no warning.

For a provenance database that is the wrong default - a mangled identifier attaches a real organisation's rows to a different EIN, and nothing downstream can detect it. md_ein() therefore returns NA for any input that is not exactly nine digits once punctuation is removed, and warns with a count. Pass strict = FALSE for ef2's truncating behaviour.

Examples

md_ein(c("123456789", "12-3456789", "EIN-12-3456789"))
#> [1] "EIN-12-3456789" "EIN-12-3456789" "EIN-12-3456789"
md_ein("EIN-00-0019818", to = "n")
#> [1] "000019818"
md_ein("19818")                       # padded: EIN-00-0019818
#> [1] "EIN-00-0019818"
suppressWarnings(md_ein("12345678901"))  # NA, not silent truncation
#> [1] NA
